messages.subject: Canopy on SNP array data
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dr. Jiang,

I was wondering if it is possible to run Canopy and build a phylogenetic
tree with copy number information only ? We have multi-regional CNA data
(Affy OncoScan) and the resulting LogR and B-allele frequency files.

--
Chloe

messages.subject: Re: [canopy_phylogeny] Canopy on SNP array data
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chloe,

Thanks for your interest in Canopy. Canopy is by default designed for next-generation sequencing data and the copy number input is generated using existing software (e.g., FALCON, Sequenza). If you can generate major and minor copy number estimates with standard error estimates I guess that would work. Another issue is that the current software does not allow copy number input only (it does allow point mutation input only). A way to solve this is to create some dummy point mutations which won’t affect the tree structure.

With this said, I would recommend call CNVs using LogR and B-allele frequency using existing software (PennCNV for example). Then visualize the results. If you don’t have too many somatic copy number changes to begin with, manual reconstruction would suffice.

Hope this is helpful,
Yuchao

messages.body_plain:
Hi Pinpin,

You can use BIC to determine the optimal number of clusters. The code is below and can be found at https://github.com/yuchaojiang/Canopy/blob/master/clustering/binomial_EM.R . A good sanity check is to plot the VAF (variant allele frequency) across samples. Sometimes you would be able to directly tell how many clusters there are from the VAF plot. See for example from https://github.com/yuchaojiang/Canopy/tree/master/clustering .

Note that this clustering is not the focus and contribution of Canopy and is thus not optimized. There are a lot other methods for clustering SNAs, such as SciClone and Pyclone, which you can refer to for a more robust clustering.

Yuchao

library(Canopy)
data(toy3)
R=toy3$R; X=toy3$X
dim(R);dim(X)
num_cluster=2:9 # Range of number of clusters to run
num_run=10 # How many EM runs per clustering step for each mutation cluster wave
canopy.cluster=canopy.cluster(R = R,
X = X,
num_cluster = num_cluster,
num_run = num_run)
# BIC to determine the optimal number of mutation clusters
bic_output=canopy.cluster$bic_output
plot(num_cluster,bic_output,xlab='Number of mutation clsuters',ylab='BIC',type='b',main='BIC for model selection')
abline(v=num_cluster[which.max(bic_output)],lty=2)

messages.subject: Formatting input
messages.body_plain:
Hi Yuchao,

I'm sorry if this is quite basic, but I'm fairly new to the field and so some of the ideas and terminology are lost on me still.
To generate the Wm and WM matrices from sequenza output, do you use the values from the mutations file output or the segments file output?
For example, the segments output has the following headers;

"chromosome" "start.pos" "end.pos" "Bf" "N.BAF" "sd.BAF" "depth.ratio" "N.ratio" "sd.ratio" "CNt" "A" "B" "LPP"

With CNt being the estimated copy number of the tumour and A and B being the estimated number of their respective alleles. But the input shown in your example matrices on page 2 of the vignettes shows values up to 3 decimal places, how to you generate those values?

I think I'm missing something obvious, but I'm unsure. Any help would be appreciated

Cheers,
Lee Brannan

messages.subject: Re: [canopy_phylogeny] Formatting input
messages.body_plain:
Hi Lee,

Thanks for your interest in Canopy! How to generate and select CNA input is outlined here:

https://github.com/yuchaojiang/Canopy/blob/master/instruction/SNA_CNA_input.md
https://github.com/yuchaojiang/Canopy/blob/master/instruction/SNA_CNA_choice.md

We recommend using Falcon or Falcon-X to generate fractional copy number input as demonstrated in the toy example. Sequenza outputs integer-value copy numbers. This is akin to knowing the truth tumor phylogeny (the observed copy numbers should always be fractional due to subpopulation mixture) besides it often times has identifiability issue with regard to purity and ploidy.

Hope that this is helpful,
Yuchao
